messages:
acme-ops: hi team, since yesterday's maintenance all our calls to the Redwood Private control plane return an mTLS handshake error. nothing in our app changed. seeing TLS alert 40 on our side.

james: on it. can you paste the client-side openssl dump and any SDK stack traces? also which region/tenant?

acme-ops: tenant id t-acme, region eu-west-1. openssl snippet: 
```
$ openssl s_client -connect api-private.redwood-acme.internal:443 -cert client.pem -key client.key -servername tenant.t-acme.private
CONNECTED(00000003)
write to 0x7f9b2c003c00 0000 - 0160 ..
140735265364608:error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure:ssl/record/rec_layer_s3.c:1544:SSL alert number 40
---
SSL handshake has read 0 bytes and written 450 bytes
---
no peer certificate available
---
```

sara: interesting that it reports "no peer certificate available". that usually means the server expected a client cert but didn’t receive one, or a middlebox terminated TLS.

lena: list of likely culprits: (1) client never sent cert (bad SDK/key), (2) intermediate CA missing so server rejected, (3) SNI mismatch routing to a non-mTLS listener, (4) TLS-terminating proxy in path.

acme-ops: we do have an outbound corporate proxy that performs TLS inspection. tcpdump on the host shows ClientHello leaving, but the proxy is a TLS-terminator.

ops-bot: collected control-plane logs for t-acme from control-plane-01 between 2024-08-12T01:00Z and 2024-08-12T08:00Z: https://internal.logs/tenant/t-acme

james: can you run a packet capture capturing the ClientHello/ServerHello exchange so we can see whether a Certificate message ever gets sent? i.e. sudo tcpdump -s0 -w /tmp/trace.pcap host api-private.redwood-acme.internal and port 443 then reproduce.

acme-ops: attached pcap. we inspected it: proxy responds with a ServerHello then requests a cert (CertificateRequest) and immediately sends a TLS alert. the upstream (from our server's perspective) never sees the client Certificate.

lena: that strongly implies the proxy is terminating TLS and not forwarding the client certificate to the upstream. the control plane then observes no client cert and aborts.

acme-ops: security team says they only allow egress via the proxy and they do SNI-based allowlists. we already added tenant.t-acme.private to their allowlist but it didn't help.

james: SNI-based allowlists can still break mTLS if the proxy performs MITM or rewrites SNI. confirm the SDK is configured to use the exact hostname in controlPlaneHost and that your openssl -servername matches.

acme-ops: yes both use tenant.t-acme.private in config and tests.

lena: two remediation paths: (A) configure proxy to do TLS passthrough for that destination (preserves client cert), (B) configure a direct egress route to control-plane IPs that bypasses TLS inspection, or (C) if unavoidable, the proxy could present its own client cert to upstream but that requires the proxy to hold customer keys (not acceptable for most customers).

acme-ops: our security team refuses to host customer private keys on the proxy. they prefer passthrough or a bypass. how many addresses do we need to open?

sara: control-plane endpoints are region-scoped and we publish a small set of IP ranges in our docs. i'll escalate to infra for the current IP list for eu-west-1 and get you a terse set of CIDRs to allow. but the recommended approach is SNI passthrough to preserve mTLS.

james: also worth checking client cert chain completeness. run: 
```
openssl verify -CAfile ca-bundle.pem -untrusted intermediate.pem client.pem
```
and ensure system clocks are in sync (skew can cause cert validation failures).

acme-ops: openssl verify returns "client.pem: OK" against our CA bundle. our clocks are accurate. control-plane logs show entries like: "tls: no client certificate".

lena: that log message plus your pcap indicates the proxy removed/terminated TLS. ask security to enable SNI passthrough for tenant.t-acme.private on port 443. also confirm the proxy doesn't rewrite the SNI header; it must pass exactly tenant.t-acme.private.

acme-ops: security made a change to passthrough based on SNI match and reported the CDN/proxy had a rule that rewrote SNI to corp-sni-outbound. they removed the rewrite and applied passthrough for our FQDN.

acme-ops: after change, openssl shows full handshake and cert chain: 
```
$ openssl s_client -connect api-private.redwood-acme.internal:443 -cert client.pem -key client.key -servername tenant.t-acme.private -showcerts
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = ACME Root CA, CN = ACME Root
verify return:1
depth=1 C = US, O = ACME Inter CA, CN = ACME Inter
verify return:1
depth=0 CN = acme-client
verify return:1
---
SSL handshake has read 3469 bytes and written 1024 bytes
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=acme-client
   i:/C=US/O=ACME Inter CA/CN=ACME Inter
---
New, TLSv1.3, Cipher is TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
```

james: thanks. can you confirm the SDK calls also succeeded after the change?

acme-ops: yes, SDK traffic is green. control plane accepted connections and mTLS auth worked. throughput normal.

sara: TL;DR for the ticket: root cause = corporate TLS inspection proxy terminated TLS and did not forward/preserve the client certificate, leading to mTLS handshake failure (server saw no client cert). remediation = enable SNI passthrough for tenant.t-acme.private or allow direct egress to Redwood control-plane IPs; do not install customer private keys on the proxy. we will update onboarding docs to call out egress/passthrough requirements and publish the region IP ranges and openssl/tcpdump tests.

lena: i'll add a short KB entry and an infra note with the exact CIDRs for eu-west-1. closing ticket contingent on your confirmation that everything remains stable for 24h.

acme-ops: confirmed stable after 6h. thanks for help. :thumbsup:
